evidence_ledger.evidence: Tara accepts only ideas with stageable hands, eyelines, props, camera distance, readable space, and imagegen-safe body logic.
evidence_ledger.visual_use: Every candidate names a concrete first frame, payoff frame, identity-safety route, and failure risk.

evidence_ledger.evidence: Slide 1 must use exactly: 'khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera'. Slide 2 should deepen the same line into an aching, comforting note; no more song lyrics may be added.

evidence_ledger.evidence: A familiar relationship truth needs a new reveal, contrast frame, close proof, viewer outcome, and protection from over-explaining.

evidence_ledger.evidence: Final illustrations require generous warm negative space for integrated readable text, identity-safe faces from real references later, and scene logic that proves the written line.

premise_lock.locked_first_slide_text: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera
premise_lock.creator_setup: The creator loves the Ghar line and wants slide 1 anchored on it, with slide 2 becoming a more emotional and comforting note on the same line.
premise_lock.visual_thesis: The house is not empty because it lacks furniture; it is empty because one exact person is not in their usual place.
premise_lock.speaker_receiver_logic: One partner is quietly saying this to the other. The scene should feel like a message someone sends to their person, not a public definition of love.
must_preserve: The feeling that one specific person is real ghar
Readable text with enough upper-middle negative space
must_reject: A typography quote-card with a house silhouette
A generic hug on a sofa with no visual proof
Any extra song lyric or continuation
Tiny phone text or object-led cleverness
Therapy-page explanation of what home means

candidates.title: The Empty Usual Spot
candidates.one_line_concept: A complete room still has one visibly unfilled place: the exact side where the other person belongs.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: Two-slide micro-carousel: slide 1 holds the lyric over a lived room with one partner and one empty habitual spot; slide 2 fills that same spot with the person, making the note feel like relief instead of explanation.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu sits low on the sofa or floor, turned toward the empty right side of the frame where Zuv usually sits. The room is otherwise complete. The lyric sits in quiet upper-middle negative space, not on a poster or wall art.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The same frame returns with Zuv occupying the empty spot, not dramatically hugging her; just close enough that the room finally reads as inhabited. The second-slide note can become a private comfort line about the house feeling full only when he is there.

visual_potential.first_frame_stop: The viewer understands absence before reading the whole line: one person, one empty place, too much room around both.
visual_potential.visual_proof: The missing habitual side proves 'tere bina' without a decorative symbol.
visual_potential.text_integration: Strong; the upper-middle space can carry the long lyric in 3-4 clean handwritten lines.
visual_potential.identity_safety: High; Aachu can be three-quarter or profile, Zuv can enter in payoff at readable medium distance without crowded face overlap.
visual_potential.prop_world: Sofa, rug, one cushion at most; no object leads the premise.

visual_evidence: Matches owned ordinary-time winner engine from DY9SfANiXWc.
Avoids the external winner-bank trap of repeating 'home is a person' as a static quote.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: People can send it as 'this is your place in my life' without typing a confession.
candidates.why_not_generic: The frame is not saying home is a person; it shows the one exact unfilled space where that person belongs.

novelty_model.contrast_frame: Not an empty house; a full house with one missing presence.

novelty_model.urgency: Emotional, not time-based: the late quiet moment when missing them becomes visible.
novelty_model.what_not_to_explain: Do not define ghar or turn the payoff into a lesson.

a_story_wrappers.caption_or_note_direction: Private, simple, sendable; no added lyric.

anti_slop_risk.repair: Keep slide 1 lonely and specific; let slide 2 comfort by filling the same exact space.

Use generous upper-middle negative space and keep background simple.
The payoff must visibly occupy the exact empty spot, not switch to a generic hug.

candidates.title: The Doorway That Still Waits
candidates.one_line_concept: The house is drawn from inside, looking toward the open doorway where the missing person should have appeared.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: Two or three slides if needed: first, a room waiting at the door; second, the comforting note lands with the person finally crossing the threshold. A third slide is optional only if story room needs a breath between ache and arrival.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Aachu stands inside near the entryway with keys still in hand, body angled toward an open but empty door. The lyric floats above the quiet interior, with the doorway low enough not to compete with text.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: Zuv appears at the threshold or just inside it, seen in medium distance. The emotional shift is not a cinematic reunion; it is the room stopping its wait.

visual_potential.first_frame_stop: The empty doorway gives immediate swipe tension: someone is expected, and they are not there yet.
visual_potential.visual_proof: The open door becomes the absence, not a metaphor pasted onto the scene.
visual_potential.text_integration: Good if the door stays lower-third and text sits in the clean upper wall space.
visual_potential.identity_safety: Medium-high; doorway depth can keep faces smaller, but payoff needs enough reference-safe detail.
visual_potential.prop_world: Keys and door only; avoid adding luggage, flowers, or dramatic rain.

visual_evidence: The illusion-of-novelty contrast is clear: not the building, the expected arrival.
A door gives readable swipe tension without microtext.
The frame can remain uncluttered for the long lyric.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: The send reason is 'I wait for you like this even when I don't say it.'
candidates.why_not_generic: It does not use a house icon or couple hug; it turns the door into a real waiting action.

candidates.title: The Call Light Is Not Enough
candidates.one_line_concept: A phone call can light the room, but it cannot fill the space where the person should be.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: Two-slide version: first, one partner on the floor or bed edge with a phone glow nearby and too much empty space; second, the same area with the person physically present, making the comfort land without needing extra words.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: Zuv or Aachu sits near a wall at night, phone face-down or screen turned away so there is no microtext. A cool rectangle of light reaches them, but the other side of the room remains empty. The lyric sits above the scene.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The payoff replaces phone-glow distance with real body presence: the other person sits beside them in the same pool of light, quiet and close, not a dramatic embrace.

visual_potential.first_frame_stop: Long-distance ache is readable without showing a chat screenshot.
visual_potential.visual_proof: The phone light proves connection is present but not enough.
visual_potential.text_integration: Strong if the night wall is plain and the phone stays low.
visual_potential.identity_safety: Medium; low light and small faces may threaten reference match if overdone.
visual_potential.prop_world: One phone only, screen content hidden.

visual_evidence: The brief's ache can be staged as distance without using more lyrics.
Phone-screen content is explicitly avoided to protect readability.
The house-style palette can handle a muted blue light accent if not too dark.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Long-distance viewers can send it as 'calls help, but I still need you here.'
candidates.why_not_generic: The phone is not the premise; it is the failed substitute for presence.

candidates.title: The Quiet Counter
candidates.one_line_concept: The kitchen has all its ordinary noise, but the counter feels wrong because the other person's place across it is empty.
candidates.suggested_slide_arc: Two-slide micro-arc: slide 1 uses a normal kitchen pause to show absence; slide 2 brings the person back into the same across-the-counter position, turning the line into comfort.
candidates.suggested_slide_1_moment: One partner stands at a small counter with hands resting still, looking at the empty opposite side rather than at the viewer. No cooking gag, no busy utensils. The lyric has clean space above.
candidates.suggested_payoff_moment: The second person occupies the opposite side of the counter in the same frame. The emotional payoff is the return of ordinary noise: a look, a leaned elbow, a familiar across-the-counter presence.

visual_potential.first_frame_stop: A kitchen should feel busy; the still hands and empty opposite side make it feel paused.
visual_potential.visual_proof: Absence is carried by eyeline and body position, not by a prop pile.
visual_potential.text_integration: Good if the counter stays lower-third and the background is spare.
visual_potential.identity_safety: Medium-high; figures can be separated and readable without face crowding.
visual_potential.prop_world: Counter only, maybe one cup; no object-led joke.

visual_evidence: Ordinary domestic setting aligns with owned A Story send behavior.
Restrained wrapper follows the current copy contract's warning against object-led invention.
Scene variety is stronger than another sofa/bed absence.
candidates.share_or_comment_trigger: Viewers who miss everyday kitchen-side companionship can send it without needing a dramatic romance caption.
candidates.why_not_generic: It makes the ache live in a paused daily habit, not a soft-focus romantic room.

top_pick.title: The Empty Usual Spot
top_pick.why_it_wins: It is the cleanest visual proof of the lyric: a complete room with one unfilled habitual place. It protects the creator's two-slide request, gives the long first-slide text room to breathe, avoids microtext and object-led cleverness, and has the strongest payoff because slide 2 can fill the exact absence slide 1 created.

scene_landing_preview_hint.first_frame_visual: One partner low in frame, facing the empty side where the other should be; text above.
scene_landing_preview_hint.swipe_reason: The viewer wants to see whether the empty space becomes comfort or stays ache.
scene_landing_preview_hint.payoff_frame: Same room, same framing, the missing person occupying the space.
scene_landing_preview_hint.share_trigger: Send to the person whose absence changes a whole room.

why_not_the_others: The Doorway That Still Waits has strong swipe tension but slightly higher scene-logic and threshold-composition risk.
The Call Light Is Not Enough is sendable for long distance but carries higher style, shadow, and phone-microtext risk.
The Quiet Counter is lived and specific, but can drift into domestic-object staging if the story room is not disciplined.

visual_risks.risk: The lyric is long enough to become cramped.
visual_risks.mitigation: Keep the figure and room in the lower half, preserve upper-middle negative space, and avoid detailed wallpaper or window clutter behind text.

visual_risks.risk: The theme can collapse into a quote-card or generic 'home is a person' poster.
visual_risks.mitigation: Require one visible body position, one unfilled habitual space, and a payoff that changes the same space.

visual_risks.risk: A sad empty-room frame can feel like grief, breakup, or abandonment instead of aching comfort.
visual_risks.mitigation: Use quiet waiting rather than devastation; make slide 2 visibly comforting and close to the same frame.

visual_risks.risk: Both faces close together in payoff can cause identity drift or crowded romance.
visual_risks.mitigation: Use medium distance, separated bodies, and reference-safe angles; do not force forehead-touch or tight hug framing.

visual_risks.risk: Scene ideas may overuse props to prove home.
visual_risks.mitigation: Let posture, eyeline, distance, and negative space carry the feeling; props stay minimal and non-premise.

slide_count_hints.reason: The creator requested two slides and the strongest visual structure is absence then comfort. A third slide would likely explain what the same-frame payoff can already make felt.
slide_count_hints.when_3_slides_could_work: Only if Story Room needs a tiny transition between ache and arrival, such as room-empty, person-waiting, person-present. This should be used only if the two-slide version feels abrupt.
slide_count_hints.why_fewer_fails: One slide would become a lyric illustration without the comforting note.
slide_count_hints.why_more_dilutes: Four or more slides would turn a clean ache into a lesson about home.
